messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: synth-canary-eu_probe_failures x8 across probes in eu-west-1. Severity: P2. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD12345

pagerduty: Notification: PagerDuty incident PD-12345 created and routed to `maria (oncall)`. Escalation policy: synth-alerts.

maria (oncall): ack'ed on PD, looking. Anyone else seeing a spike in canary failures? :eyes:

alex (sre): I'm seeing duplicate probe fanout in the prober logs right now. Probes are being scheduled 8x for the same check id. Example log snippet: `probe_id=canary-72 attempt=1` then immediately `probe_id=canary-72 attempt=2..8`

ravi (eng-prober): digging in prober controller. We deployed a change to the sampling/routing config ~30m ago. Rolling back now to previous config. Patch: revert commit `c4a9f2f` which introduced `fanout_multiplier`.

sophia (eng-runtime): can confirm the new flag `fanout_multiplier=10` was shipped accidentally in the eu prober config via the k8s ConfigMap `prober-config-eu`. That would amplify a single failing probe into multiple failing requests.

maria (oncall): ok that explains the noise. Is this causing real customer impact or just alert noise?

alex (sre): initial check of production ingress metrics: no increase in 5xx or latency for customer traffic. This looks like synthetic-only. I ran a quick query: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{env=prod,status=~"5..",job="frontends"}[5m]))` — stable.

ravi (eng-prober): rollback completed, restarted prober deployment `prober-eu` (kubectl rollout restart deploy/prober-eu). Logs show fanout back to 1. Re-run single probe: OK.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-12345 acknowledged by maria (oncall).

maria (oncall): thanks. I'll keep this thread open until we confirm no more duplicate failures for the next 30m. Can someone add root cause/mitigation notes for the postmortem?

sophia (eng-runtime): root cause: mis-rolled config change that set `fanout_multiplier` to 10 in `prober-config-eu`. Mitigation: rolled back ConfigMap, added a guard in deployment pipeline to reject `fanout_multiplier > 2` for prober configs. Follow-up: create an alert for abrupt change in probe fanout multiplier.

alex (sre): also adding a short-term runbook entry: if probe failures spike without customer impact, check `prober-config-*` for `fanout_multiplier` and the last configmap change.

ravi (eng-prober): note: I saw some PagerDuty duplicate incidents because the prober emitted unique failing run ids per fanout. We need to dedupe at alerting layer for identical check ids within a 1m window. Filed TODO: PD dedupe rule and PR #452 in monitoring repo.

maria (oncall): good. Customer impact: None observed (synthetic-only). Severity demoted to info in our internal tracker. We'll still do postmortem to avoid recurrence.

oncall-handoff-bot: Reminder: on-call handoff at 06:00 UTC. maria (oncall) — please add notes to the handoff if still investigating.

maria (oncall): will add summary and link to PD in the handoff. TL;DR: accidental config change -> duplicate probe fanout -> alert storm. Fixed by rollback; added pipeline guard + PD dedupe task.

alex (sre): closing PD incident now. If any flapping returns, re-open thread. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: PD-12345 resolved by maria (oncall).
__note: This file is a synthetic Slack thread representing an incident coordination conversation involving PagerDuty and an incident bot about synthetic canary probe fanout duplication. All fields are strings or lists of strings as required.
